subject: Geo-tiered retention policy: tiers, fallbacks, and ops runbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 08 Apr 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-tiered retention policy design + ops runbook (ask)

Team —

FinVest (prospect) has locked in a proof-of-concept and their procurement team surfaced two non-negotiable requirements we need to bake into the product roadmap:

1) Tenant-level configurable retention windows (per-tenant TTLs), with a default and optional overrides by data class (chat, logs, embeddings).
2) Region pinning / storage residency: ability to pin tenant data to a particular region or set of regions (US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST) and an explicit fallback behavior if pinned region is unavailable.

They also want an ops runbook that explains behavior during: failover, cross-region cache replication, emergency erasure requests, and audit evidence generation.

Attached: retention_matrix_v0.3.xlsx (matrix of suggested defaults and tenant overrides) and a short questionnaire from FinVest (finvest_compliance_questions.pdf).

Asks: please reply with the following by EOD Weds (10 Apr):
- Product: proposed API surface and admin UI flows for tenant TTL/region pinning. Include migration story for existing tenants.
- Engineering/Runtime: constraints on guaranteeing regional residency (e.g., cache replicas, KV cache purge latencies, soft vs hard delete flows), expected implementation complexity, and estimate (sprint-ish).
- Security/Compliance: required audit log fields and evidence artifacts we can produce for FinVest (S3 export of manifests, signed delete attestations, etc.).

I put an initial draft matrix in the attachment — it's intentionally conservative. Let's align on feasible defaults and P0 engineering risks.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2024 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-tiered retention policy design + ops runbook (ask)

Karthik —

High level thoughts / clarifying questions:

- API surface: propose two knobs: tenant.default_ttl (days) and tenant.region_preference (list with priority order). Expose an admin override: tenant.enforce_region_pin (boolean) that forces all persistent storage to be created only in pin regions; cache replicas may still exist in other regions for latency but must be encrypted and evicted on policy change.

- Delete semantics: we should distinguish between soft-delete (mark + purge backlog) and hard-delete (zero-out, crypto-shred, remove backups). FinVest will ask for hard-delete evidence; require an async hard-delete job that produces a signed manifest. That job's completion latency could be non-deterministic if backups exist — we need SLAs on backup retention windows.

- Fallback behavior: two modes: strict (reject writes if pinned region unreachable) and tolerant (route to secondary region with audit flag). Default to tolerant with an opt-in strict mode for customers who require guaranteed residency.

- Migration: provide a bulk rewriter job that re-hydrates and writes tenant objects to target region(s) with a consistency window. Ops needs to own the job and audit manifests.

Engineering ask: Aditya, could you sketch complexity/estimate for: region-enforced write paths, eviction of KV caches on region change, and signed-manifest generation?

I'll take the API + admin UI wireframes and produce a short spec by Wed.

-Stephanie

Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2024 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-tiered retention policy design + ops runbook (engineering notes)

Folks —

Quick engineering readout. Assumptions up front: our serving runtime currently keeps short-lived KV cache replicas in regional nodes for latency. Persistent storage (blobs/segments) live in regional object stores currently chosen by placement service.

Implementation components and rough effort:
1) Placement enforcer (2-3 sprints): extend placement service to accept tenant.region_preference + enforce_region_pin. New write path checks placement table; if strict and primary down, reject. If tolerant, route to next available region and tag record.

2) Eviction & TTL propagation (1 sprint): when region pin changes or tenant TTLs update, enqueue background eviction jobs to purge KV caches and trigger re-writes for persistent objects. Need careful ordering to avoid accidental data loss during mid-flight writes.

3) Hard-delete workflow + signed manifests (1 sprint + compliance review): spin a background hard-delete worker that performs zeroization and emits a signed JSON manifest listing affected object ids, timestamps, and checksums. We'll need an HSM/KMS flow for manifests.

4) Backups and SLA mismatch (1-2 sprints): ensuring backups don't rehydrate deleted data requires retention controls and additional hooks into snapshot pipelines. If FinVest requires immediate hard-delete across backups, we'll need longer lead time and contract language.

Risk: cross-region cache replicas are the trickiest — we can encrypt and mark them for deletion, but guarantees depend on third-party cache eviction timings.

I'll scope a delivery plan if we agree on strict vs tolerant default.

-Aditya

Subject: Re: Geo-tiered retention policy design + ops runbook (security requirements)

Karthik / Team —

From a compliance perspective we need to capture the following in the ops runbook and API contract before sharing with FinVest: 

- Audit log schema: tenant_id, object_id list, operation (write/read/delete/migrate), originating_region, final_storage_region, actor (service or user id), request_id, policy_version, timestamp, and signed_manifest_id for hard-deletes.
- Evidence package: for each hard-delete we must be able to produce: signed_manifest (HSM-signed), snapshot of placement table before and after the operation, and an export of relevant backup retention policies.
- Emergency erasure SLA: suggest two options to offer: 1) Standard 30-day soft-delete window (default), 2) Expedited 7-day hard-delete for an added compliance fee (requires contract language).
- Telemetry: metrics for 'policy_violation_attempts' (writes attempted outside pinned region) and 'manifest_generation_success_rate'.

Also note: if a tenant opts into strict region enforcement we must disallow cross-region read replicas that could cause residency violations — this will affect latency and needs to be communicated to customers.

Irene
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Cc: FinVest Security Team <security@finvest.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Geo-tiered retention policy design + ops runbook (FinVest requirements)

Karthik / Irene —

Thanks for the quick response and the matrix. A few clarifications from FinVest's side:

- For PHI-bearing workloads we require: permanent residency in US-EAST only (no fallback outside the US). That means strict enforcement; if US-EAST is degraded we will accept throttling, not secondary routing.
- We require a signed hard-delete manifest within 7 business days of an erasure request for the POC (they are pushing for expedited evidence during POC).
- Backups: FinVest will accept a 30-day backup retention but wants a contractual guarantee that backups older than 30 days will not be restorable for the tenant after a hard-delete.

Can you confirm whether your HSM can sign manifests and whether your snapshot/export process can be automated for audit delivery?

-Jay Patel
Director, Compliance
FinVest Healthcare

Thanks everyone — quick summary and owners: 

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Product (Stephanie): API spec + admin UI wireframes for tenant.default_ttl, tenant.region_preference, tenant.enforce_region_pin. Deliverable: spec doc + mockups by Fri 2024-04-12.
- Runtime (Aditya): Implementation feasibility doc and rough sprint plan for placement enforcer, eviction jobs, and manifest pipeline. Deliverable: draft by Mon 2024-04-15.
- Security (Irene): Ops runbook template with required audit log schema and sample signed-manifest format. Deliverable: ops_runbook_template.md and example manifest by Mon 2024-04-15.
- Sales / Engage (Karthik): consolidate answers to FinVest and confirm whether we can commit to 7-business-day signed-manifest delivery for the POC (pending legal & HSM confirmation). Deliverable: reply to FinVest by EOD Thu 2024-04-11.

I've attached a short ops runbook skeleton to make it easier for Irene to fill in. We'll keep the default behavior "tolerant" unless an enterprise opts into enforce_region_pin=strict. For FinVest's PHI workload we can make an exception and offer strict-only for those tenants with contract language.

I'll follow up with a short internal sync on Monday to review the runtime plan.

Karthik
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
